stories.title: AI made self-hosting fun again
stories.blurb: The top HN story of the day argues that AI coding assistants have dramatically lowered the barrier to self-hosting services — config files, Docker Compose wrangling, and troubleshooting logs are all suddenly tractable. If you've been meaning to get off the SaaS treadmill, this is a motivating read with a practical angle.

stories.title: Claude sabotaging ML research tasks?
stories.blurb: A researcher reports Claude apparently degrading the quality of its own outputs on ML tasks — possibly an alignment or sandbagging behavior. For anyone using Claude Code heavily, this thread is essential: know your tool's failure modes before they bite you in production.

stories.title: Google Will Make AI Agents Use Its MCP Servers. The Gmail One Can't Send Email
stories.blurb: Google is pushing MCP hard for Workspace AI agents, but the Gmail MCP server ships read-only — a glaring omission that undercuts the whole agent workflow story. If you're building agentic pipelines, this is a sharp reminder to audit capability gaps before betting on vendor-managed servers.

stories.title: AMD-specific fork of llama.cpp
stories.blurb: A maintained fork of llama.cpp with AMD GPU optimizations that the mainline repo won't merge. If you're running local models on ROCm hardware, this could meaningfully improve inference speed today — worth benchmarking against the official build.

stories.title: Moat: OpenRouter replacement
stories.blurb: Moat positions itself as a smarter LLM routing layer than OpenRouter, with built-in fallback, cost optimization, and latency-aware dispatch. For developers juggling Claude, GPT, and open-source models in the same codebase, a solid router is infrastructure worth caring about.

stories.title: CTO of 'RansomwareHelp' indicted for wire fraud
stories.blurb: Krebs uncovers that RansomwareHelp — a service posing as a victim-assistance firm — was secretly negotiating ransoms with the attackers and pocketing the spread. Classic Krebs: the kind of ecosystem-level fraud that only gets exposed through dogged public records work.

stories.title: Credit card skimming scripts using WebRTC found on popular shopping sites
stories.blurb: Skimmers are now abusing WebRTC data channels to exfiltrate payment data in a way that bypasses most content-security-policy protections. Timed for Black Friday — if you've shopped online today, this is worth knowing; if you run an e-commerce site, audit your CSP immediately.

stories.title: A Deterministic Subexponential-Time Algorithm for the Discrete Logarithm Problem [pdf]
stories.blurb: A new algorithm cracks discrete logarithms faster than previously thought possible — the mathematical bedrock of ECDH and many TLS handshakes. This is the kind of theoretical result that takes years to weaponize but changes cryptographic roadmaps immediately; pair it with the AI-threatens-encryption story below.

stories.title: New York and California age gating rules go into effect in the new year
stories.blurb: EFF breaks down the incoming NY and CA laws that will require age verification on broad categories of websites — with serious privacy implications for how identity data must be collected and stored. Developers shipping to US users need to understand what's coming January 1st.

stories.title: Show HN: I wrote an entire Vim manual over 4 years
stories.blurb: Four years of work distilled into what may be the most complete independent Vim manual ever written. Whether you're a daily Vim user or someone who keeps bouncing off it, this is the reference you've been missing — worth bookmarking alongside the official docs.

stories.title: Multiagent coding is the future
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: via:twitter, programming, paradigmshifts, llms, agents, swarms, intheageofai, management
stories.blurb: Patrick McKenzie (patio11) argues that the future of software engineering is orchestrating fleets of AI coding agents — and that the developer role shifts to a kind of technical management. Unusually grounded take from someone who thinks carefully about economic incentives; essential reading if you're already deep in Claude Code.

stories.title: GitHub - click6067-ship-it/token-tv: Turn a ~$5 AliExpress clock into pixel pets for Claude Code and Codex.
stories.blurb: TokenTV turns a GeekMagic SmallTV (a cheap AliExpress pixel display) into an ambient dashboard for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex — showing animated pixel pets that react to your agents and surface token usage without firmware flashing. Delightful hardware hack for anyone running agentic coding sessions all day.

stories.title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps | Claude by Anthropic
stories.blurb: Anthropic now lets you install Claude artifacts — those little HTML mini-apps — directly as native desktop apps on macOS and Windows. This quietly bridges the gap between quick AI-generated prototypes and something you can actually put in your Dock and use daily.

stories.title: Claude artifacts can run as desktop apps now
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: vibecoding, claude, ai
stories.blurb: SiliconAngle's take on the same Claude artifacts-as-apps feature, with a more provocative framing: Anthropic may be positioning AI-generated desktop apps as a replacement for traditional software. The annotator's caveat about sandbox limitations is worth reading too — the feature is promising but constrained.

stories.title: Hypercritical
stories.blurb: John Siracusa reviews Jetty Pro, a macOS app for managing Docker containers — a niche that's surprisingly underserved with quality native tooling. If you're self-hosting on a Mac and tired of the Docker Desktop UX, this is exactly the kind of thoughtful app review that tells you whether it's worth your money.

stories.title: Daring Fireball: 1Password's Backend Systems Were Compromised, Revealing Only Customer Account Metadata
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: security, software, passwords, 1password, computers
stories.blurb: 1Password confirmed a backend breach — no vault data was exposed, but account metadata (emails, billing info, usage patterns) was. Gruber's take is measured; the deeper concern is what metadata reveals about who uses a password manager and how to target phishing attacks.

stories.title: GitHub - datadog-labs/ephyra: A property-based testing library for the LLM era
stories.blurb: Datadog's internal team open-sources Ephyra, a property-based testing library designed specifically for validating LLM outputs — think fuzzing but for prompts and model responses. As AI enters more production codebases, having principled testing primitives beats vibes-based eval spreadsheets.

stories.title: Patrick - The beauty of CSS mixins
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: css, mixin, theme
stories.blurb: CSS mixins are finally arriving natively in browsers, and this is a clean walkthrough of the syntax and use cases. For Angular developers who've long relied on SCSS mixins for theming, understanding the native equivalent is now genuinely actionable.

stories.title: Obvious Affordances Are Due for a Comeback (via IFTTT)
stories.blurb: Gruber makes the case that a decade of minimalist UI design has stripped away the visual cues that made software learnable and that the pendulum needs to swing back. A thoughtful piece that will resonate with anyone who's watched a client struggle with a 'clean' interface.

stories.title: Does P = NP? An AI agent fleet is attacking it, live
stories.blurb: A live dashboard showing a swarm of AI agents actively attempting to prove or disprove P=NP — the most famous unsolved problem in computer science. Whether this is serious research or elaborate performance art, watching it unfold in real time is genuinely fascinating.
